newsitem.title: RUSSIA: OSCE gives seal of approval to Chechnya poll.
newsitem.headline: OSCE gives seal of approval to Chechnya poll.

text.p: A representative from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe said on Tuesday the Chechen presidential elections were free and fair.

"On the basis of all available information the election expressed the free will of eligible voters," Tim Guldimann, the head of OSCE mission in Chechnya, told a news conference. He described the election, held on Monday, as "legitimate".

Altogether 12 candidates contested the polls, called after Moscow and Chechen separatist rebels struck a peace deal on August 31 that ended Russia's 21-month military campaign to subdue the southern region's independence bid.
The Chechen electoral commission was expected to announce first official results of the polls later on Tuesday but Aslan Maskhadov, seen as a moderate candidate, has already claimed victory.

President Boris Yeltsin's press secretary said the Kremlin leader had cautiously welcomed Maskhadov's apparent win and hoped that this would help further peace talks. But he made clear Moscow still ruled out full independence for Chechnya.
Maskhadov told a news conference in the Chechen capital, Grozny, that he was firm in his demand for full independence and was ready to start talks with Moscow to achieve it.
